Appointment Scheduling Guidelines for Post-Surgical Patients

This document provides guidance for scheduling and attending post-surgical follow-up appointments. Attending all scheduled appointments is essential for a safe and effective recovery.

Scheduling Your Appointments:
Before discharge from the hospital, your care team will typically schedule your first post-operative appointment. Bring your insurance card and photo identification to every appointment. If you do not have your appointment details at the time of discharge, contact the surgeon's office within 24 hours of arriving home to schedule your follow-up.

Standard Appointment Schedule After Total Knee Replacement:
- Post-operative Day 10–14: Wound check and staple/suture removal
- 6 Weeks Post-Operative: Range of motion and functional assessment
- 3 Months Post-Operative: Functional milestone review and imaging if indicated
- 6 Months Post-Operative: Implant stability review
- 1 Year Post-Operative: Annual implant and functional review

What to Bring to Each Appointment:
Bring the following items to every follow-up visit: a current list of all medications (prescription, over-the-counter, and supplements), your insurance information, any X-ray films or imaging CDs if provided, a list of questions or concerns you want to discuss, and your physical therapy progress notes if available.

Preparing for Your Appointment:
Arrange transportation in advance, as you may not be cleared to drive for several weeks after surgery. Wear comfortable, loose-fitting clothing that allows easy access to the surgical leg. Arrive 15 minutes early to complete any check-in paperwork. If your mobility is limited, inform the office in advance so they can arrange appropriate seating and assistance.

Rescheduling and Cancellation Policy:
Contact the surgeon's office at least 24 hours in advance if you need to reschedule a non-urgent appointment. Do not cancel appointments without rescheduling, as delayed follow-up can put your recovery at risk. For urgent concerns between scheduled appointments, call the surgeon's after-hours line or go to the nearest emergency room if needed.

Telehealth Appointments:
Some post-operative appointments may be conducted via telehealth (video call) depending on your surgeon's preferences and your recovery stage. Telehealth visits are typically suitable for reviewing lab results, discussing medication adjustments, and answering general questions. Physical examinations and imaging must be done in-person.

Coordinating with Other Providers:
If you are seeing multiple providers (e.g., your primary care physician, a cardiologist, a physical therapist), ensure each provider is informed of your recent surgery and current medication list. Share your surgical discharge summary with all providers involved in your care. Good communication between providers helps prevent medication errors and conflicting advice.

Blood Work and Lab Appointments:
If you are taking warfarin (Coumadin), you will need regular INR (International Normalized Ratio) blood tests to monitor your anticoagulation level. These tests may be done at a dedicated anticoagulation clinic, your primary care office, or a laboratory. Your target INR range will be specified by your surgeon. Keep a record of your INR results and share them at every appointment.

Emergency Appointments:
If you experience any warning signs described in the Warning Signs After Surgery document, do not wait for your next scheduled appointment. Contact your surgeon's office immediately for an urgent appointment, or go directly to the emergency room if your symptoms are severe or sudden.
